output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed incidents reaching the category were 37 in September and 36 in October, in line with the earlier ~38 a month. Forty-seven of them were then moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" a few minutes after the 3.5-hour SLA warning. A script on a Brackwater analyst host did this, using the integration account that was given edit rights at migration. These cases then drop out of the incident count and the containment metrics. That explains the 100% SLA figure, the faster average containment time, and the growing monitoring queue (about 40 to 96). It is not a platform fault, because the connector wrote no categories. It is not a drop in attacks or in alert volume. I have not established whether the 28 deprecated rules missed attacks. Do not cut the IR retainer and do not pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have Corvane's team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove the integration account's category-edit rights. Also review the 96-case queue. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation and keep the service credits in reserve until the contract is checked. I'm fairly confident in the main finding, less so on intent and on the rules question.
